title: Rectangular prism
spec:
Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and a translation vector of [0.259, 0.5882, 0.0]. Next, draw the first face of the rectangular prism. Begin with the first loop, which consists of four lines. The first line starts at [0.0, 0.0] and ends at [0.113, 0.0]. The second line starts at [0.113, 0.0] and ends at [0.113, 0.0709]. The third line starts at [0.113, 0.0709] and ends at [0.0, 0.0709]. Finally, the fourth line starts at [0.0, 0.0709] and ends at [0.0, 0.0].

For the second face, create another loop with four lines. The first line starts at [0.1183, 0.001] and ends at [0.2313, 0.001]. The second line starts at [0.2313, 0.001] and ends at [0.2313, 0.0719]. The third line starts at [0.2313, 0.0719] and ends at [0.1183, 0.0719]. The fourth line starts at [0.1183, 0.0719] and ends at [0.1183, 0.001].

After drawing both faces, apply a scaling factor of 0.2313 to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Transform the two-dimensional sketch into three-dimensional space using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and the translation vector [0.259, 0.5882, 0.0]. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch along the normal direction by 0.0806 units, ensuring that no extrusion occurs in the opposite direction. Create a new solid body from this extrusion. The dimensions of the rectangular prism are length: 0.23130101690756932 units, width: 0.0718622171657285 units, and height: 0.08057457180371386 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
wp = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the first face (face_1)
face_1 = wp.moveTo(0, 0) \
           .lineTo(0.113, 0) \
           .lineTo(0.113, 0.0709) \
           .lineTo(0, 0.0709) \
           .close()

# Define the second face (face_2)
face_2 = wp.moveTo(0.1183, 0.001) \
           .lineTo(0.2313, 0.001) \
           .lineTo(0.2313, 0.0719) \
           .lineTo(0.1183, 0.0719) \
           .close()

# Combine the faces to form a single sketch
sketch = face_1.add(face_2)

# Extrude the sketch
extrusion = sketch.extrude(0.0806)

# Apply the translation
r = extrusion.translate((0.259, 0.5882, 0))

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch for the first face
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0719, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0719, 0.0806) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0806) \
     .close()

# Define the sketch for the second face
r = r.moveTo(0.0719, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.2313, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.2313, 0.0806) \
     .lineTo(0.0719, 0.0806) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create the cube
r = r.extrude(0.0719)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, so we need to use rotation matrices
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

import cadquery as cq

# Overall bounding box: X 0.2313, Y 0.0719, Z 0.0806
# The part consists of two rectangular blocks side by side along X,
# separated by a small gap, with the right block slightly shorter.

block_w = 0.113          # width of each block along X
gap = 0.2313 - 2 * block_w  # gap between the blocks (~0.0053)
depth = 0.0719           # Y depth
h_left = 0.0806          # height of left (taller) block
h_right = 0.0790         # height of right (slightly shorter) block

# Left block (base on Z=0)
left = cq.Workplane("XY").box(block_w, depth, h_left, centered=(True, True, False)) \
    .translate((block_w / 2.0, 0, 0))

# Right block (base on Z=0), offset by block width plus gap
right = cq.Workplane("XY").box(block_w, depth, h_right, centered=(True, True, False)) \
    .translate((block_w + gap + block_w / 2.0, 0, 0))

# Combine the two separate-looking bodies
r = left.union(right)
